reception: Reception lies less in other compilers than in computer architecture. Hardware proposals for irregular memory access cite milk as the software point of comparison: PHI differentiates its approach from milk's, täkō measures against it as a baseline, DX100 reuses its workloads, and a survey of sparse-matrix accelerators picks up the idea. Peripheral mentions cluster in the same territory — locality-enhancing systems from hardware-accelerated graph-traversal scheduling to SpMV vectorization list DRAM-conscious clustering among software answers to the random-access problem. The record is small but placed where the technique aimed: papers about making indirect references cheap.
